title: Development and Evaluation of a Digital Individualized Guidance Instrument for Patients Undergoing CAR-T Cell Therapy in Saxony
summary:
Complications can occur after CAR T-cell therapy, both during the hospital stay and after discharge. The study aims to investigate whether regularly recording symptoms and health data using a study app and a smartwatch is feasible and how patients feel about this digital support.
Participants regularly record their symptoms and complete the scheduled tests using the app. In addition, a smartwatch records various health and activity data. This digital support complements usual medical care and does not replace it.
The data collected will help us better understand changes and potential complications after CAR T-cell therapy and may help identify them earlier in the future.
Digital support usually continues until day 90 after CAR T-cell therapy. For a small group of patients diagnosed with multiple myeloma, it will continue for up to one year after treatment as part of the study.
conditions: Other and unspecified types of non-Hodgkin lymphoma
Multiple myeloma and malignant plasma cell neoplasms
Other neoplasms of uncertain or unknown behaviour of lymphoid, haematopoietic and related tissue

interventions.name: Following informed consent and study enrollment, a digital baseline assessment is performed before the start of CAR T-cell therapy. From the time of CAR T-cell infusion, an extended Immune Effector Cell-Associated Encephalopathy (ICE) score and symptoms are recorded regularly via the “CARTox” study

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Indication for CAR T-cell therapy, as determined in the context of routine clinical care
Exclusion criteria:
•	Lack of capacity to provide informed consent
•	Language barrier
•	Cognitive or physical limitations preventing meaningful use of the app or smartwatch
